reference_use.conclusion: The local snapshot (project b4d606d, Mathlib 25730c7c) has no counterpart for the contract's IMRep push-forward, first variation or mean curvature, so the twelve children are new. The library facts they reuse are the ones cited in the child proofs. The only blocking defect from v1 is confirmed and repaired. Mathlib's exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt takes r : (E →L[ℝ] F) → ℝ≥0 with rpos : ∀ A, r A ≠ 0, and the unit-sphere minimum used in v1 does not exist for n = 0. The fix sets m(A) = 1 for n = 0 (alternatively 1/K from LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith, which also covers subsingleton domains) and r = 1 on non-injective maps; rpos then holds for every A. pieces_check compiles the resulting bi-Lipschitz partition for all n and P using only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The n = 0 facts used in the new step 10 exist: Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero, Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton, LinearMap.normDet_of_subsingleton and Matrix.det_isEmpty. The upper-density lemma needs only real n ≥ 0, and the SimonGMT area lemmas have no rank hypothesis and accept arbitrary weights. All twelve child types (eleven identical to v1) elaborate after import GMT.Ch07.Submission and also with the contract inlined. minimizing_implies_stationary compiles from them, and the conditional assembly uses only standard axioms. subproblem.title: Simon Ch. 4, 2.7 and 3.14: stationarity in N ∩ U gives locally bounded generalized mean curvature
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, N an embedded C² d-dimensional submanifold with (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U with H^n(M ∖ N) = 0 whose varifold v(M, θ) is stationary in N ∩ U (R.IsStationaryAlong N). Then v(M, θ) has a generalized mean curvature H in U (Simon Ch. 4, 3.14): H is μ_V-measurable, bounded on every compact subset of U, and ∫_M θ div_M X dH^n = −∫ X·H dμ_V for every X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^P), μ_V = θH^n⌞M (R.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n d : ℕ) (U N : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 d N → (closure N \ N) ∩ U = ∅ → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ N) = 0 → R.IsStationaryAlong N → R.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 4, 2.7 and 3.14 with Ch. 2, 5.9 (div_M X = div_M X^T − X·H_N), i.e. step 6 of the parent proof. Siblings: chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv (TS), imrep_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm (TM), approxTangent_le_submanifold_tangentSpace (H1), submanifold_tangentProjection_c1_extension (EXT).
1. Notation. μ := μHE[n].restrict M, μ_V := R.measure = θ·μ, p(x) := starProjection(approxTangentPlane n M x), div_M Y(x) := tangentialDivergence n M Y x = trace(p(x)∘DY(x)). N ∩ U = N̄ ∩ U (from (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅) is relatively closed in U and Borel. By TS, tangentSpace N z is a linear subspace for z ∈ N, so span(tangentSpace N z) = tangentSpace N z.
2. Extension. EXT gives an open O ⊇ N and pr, C¹ on O, with pr(z) = P_N(z) := starProjection(tangentSpace N z) for z ∈ N; P_N(z) is self-adjoint, idempotent, with range tangentSpace N z.
3. Definition of H. H(x) := Σ_{j=1}^P (Dpr(x)[p(x)e_j])*(p(x)e_j) for x ∈ N ∩ U, and H(x) := 0 otherwise; here Dpr(x) = fderiv ℝ pr x : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P), (·)* is the adjoint and (e_j) the standard basis. (At the good points of step 6 this is Σ_i B_x(τ_i, τ_i), the trace over T_xM of the second fundamental form of N, as in the parent proof; this identification is not needed.)
4. Measurability. x ↦ fderiv ℝ pr x is measurable (Mathlib measurable_fderiv); x ↦ p(x) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (TM); (A, q) ↦ Σ_j (A(qe_j))*(qe_j) is continuous; N ∩ U is Borel. Hence H is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and so μ_V-a.e. strongly measurable (μ_V ≪ μ).
5. Local bound. Let K ⊆ U be compact. K ∩ N is compact (relatively closed in K) and contained in O, where Dpr is continuous (pr is C¹ on the open set O), so Λ_0 := sup_{K∩N} ‖Dpr‖ < ∞. For x ∈ K ∩ N, ‖H(x)‖ ≤ Σ_j ‖Dpr(x)‖·|p(x)e_j|² ≤ PΛ_0; for x ∈ K ∖ N, H(x) = 0. So ‖H(x)‖ ≤ Λ := PΛ_0 for every x ∈ K, in particular μ_V-a.e. on K.
6. Good points. G := {x ∈ M ∩ N ∩ U : ∃ Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q}. μ(M ∖ G) = 0, because M ⊆ U, μHE[n](M ∖ N) = 0 and R.orients provides approximate tangent planes μ-a.e. For x ∈ G, Q(x) := approxTangentPlane n M x is an approximate tangent plane of M at x, and by H1 (N is in particular an embedded C¹ submanifold, as C² charts are C¹) Q(x) ⊆ tangentSpace N x; thus P_N(x)u = u for u ∈ Q(x).
7. Tangential part. Fix X ∈ C¹(ℝ^P; ℝ^P) with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ U; K_X := tsupport X. K_X ∩ N is compact and ⊆ O ∩ U (open), so there is χ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, tsupport χ ⊆ O ∩ U and χ = 1 on an open neighbourhood V_X of K_X ∩ N. Let X^T(y) := χ(y)·pr(y)(X(y)). X^T is C¹ on O (products and compositions of C¹ maps) and vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ tsupport χ; these two open sets cover ℝ^P, so X^T is C¹, with compact support and tsupport X^T ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ U. For z ∈ N ∩ U, X^T(z) = χ(z)P_N(z)X(z) ∈ tangentSpace N z. Hence R.IsStationaryAlong N gives R.firstVariation X^T = 0.
8. Normal part. Y := X − X^T is C¹ with compact support. Claim: for x ∈ G, div_M Y(x) = −⟨X(x), H(x)⟩. Write p := p(x); trace(p∘DY(x)) = trace(p∘DY(x)∘p) = Σ_j ⟨pe_j, DY(x)(pe_j)⟩. (a) If x ∉ K_X: X ≡ 0 on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K_X ∋ x, so X^T ≡ 0 there, DY(x) = 0 and X(x) = 0; both sides vanish. (b) If x ∈ K_X: then x ∈ K_X ∩ N ⊆ V_X, and on the open set V_X ∩ O ∋ x, Y(y) = X(y) − pr(y)(X(y)); so DY(x)h = DX(x)h − (Dpr(x)h)(X(x)) − pr(x)(DX(x)h). For u ∈ Q(x) ⊆ tangentSpace N x: ⟨u, DX(x)u − P_N(x)DX(x)u⟩ = ⟨u − P_N(x)u, DX(x)u⟩ = 0, hence ⟨u, DY(x)u⟩ = −⟨u, (Dpr(x)u)X(x)⟩ = −⟨(Dpr(x)u)*u, X(x)⟩. Summing over u = pe_j gives div_M Y(x) = −⟨Σ_j (Dpr(x)[pe_j])*(pe_j), X(x)⟩ = −⟨X(x), H(x)⟩, since x ∈ N ∩ U.
9. Integral identity. All integrands are μ-a.e. strongly measurable (TM for the divergences, step 4 for H) and bounded by a constant times θ·1_{K'} for the compact set K' := K_X ∪ tsupport χ ⊆ U, hence μ-integrable (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). As DX = DX^T + DY and the trace is linear, R.firstVariation X = R.firstVariation X^T + ∫_M θ div_M Y dH^n = 0 − ∫_M θ⟨X, H⟩ dH^n (step 8, μ-a.e.) = −∫ ⟨X, H⟩ dμ_V (integral against the density θ). Together with steps 4 and 5 this is R.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature. (For n = 0, p ≡ 0, so H = 0 and both sides vanish.)
proof_key_steps: Extend P_N to a C¹ field pr near N (EXT) and set X^T := χ·pr·X, a C¹_c(U) field tangent to N, so δV(X^T) = 0 by stationarity.
At a.e. x ∈ M (x ∈ N, T_xM ⊆ T_xN by H1) div_M(X − X^T)(x) = −X(x)·H(x) with H(x) = Σ_j (Dpr(x)[p e_j])*(p e_j).
H is measurable (TM) and bounded on compact subsets of U (continuity of Dpr on the compact K ∩ N); integrate to get δV(X) = −∫X·H dμ_V.

audit.reason: The explicit derivative-of-projection formula supplies measurable H and compact-set bounds. The cutoff field is an admissible tangential test field; tangent inclusion and the trace computation give the required integral identity. This establishes the selected parent's second conclusion without circular reliance.
